name: Soy sauce and fermented seasoning sauces

iAs.rationale: No sovereign inorganic-arsenic ML exists for soy sauce; total arsenic is governed at 1000 (Vietnam 'Sauce'). Inorganic arsenic is controlled by reflex speciation on any elevated total arsenic.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; reflex iAs speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on any total-As exceedance.

MeHg.rationale: No methylation pathway and no fish source in a soy/wheat ferment.

Ni.rationale: No sovereign nickel ML exists for soy sauce, but soybeans are strong nickel accumulators (EU regulates soybean nickel at 15000) and the ferment is soy-derived, so a real source pathway exists. Held under a reflex screen.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on each lot; monitored under ALARA against the tightest available food nickel context.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign total-chromium ML exists for soy sauce; the only food chromium MLs in the register are dairy. Rebuttable and audited each build.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS screen; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number for a food; it is the reflex-speciation species. Any total-chromium exceedance is speciated, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Sn.rationale: Tin migrates only from tinplate cans; soy sauce is sold in glass or plastic, not tinplate. No non-canned tin pathway exists.

Al.rationale: No sovereign aluminium ML exists for soy sauce and no aluminium pathway operates. Rebuttable and audited each build.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; face value, no reconstitution; read-across / control / not-material for unregulated cells; no occurrence percentiles)
lineage_note: Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning SAUCE, so the Vietnam QCVN 8-2 generic 'Sauce' MLs govern directly (Pb 2000, Cd 1000, tAs 1000, tHg 50) — corroborated by the Singapore 'tomato ketchup and other sauces' finished-sauce ML (Pb 2000 / tAs 1000). These are loose ceilings flagged for the occurrence ratchet; soy sauce has a documented lead-contamination history (e.g. Hong Kong recalls). Nickel is held under a soy-accumulation screen because soybeans concentrate nickel (EU regulates soybean nickel at 15000) and no sovereign sets a sauce nickel ML.
